subject: Private deployment: key custody, operator telemetry & emergency access
messages:
From: Sara Holt <sara.holt@medicahealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Medica Legal <legal@medicahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Jun 2025 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on private deployment privacy terms — keys & access

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we evaluate Redwood for a private deployment, Legal asked me to capture a couple of high-level questions so we can align on the DPA and deployment model before we proceed to a procurement term sheet. Can you confirm the following?

- Key custody options: does Redwood support customer-owned keys (BYOK) for on-prem and VPC deployments? If so, do you require escrow or can customers hold CMKs exclusively?
- Operator access: what level of operator/admin access does Redwood support for breakglass support events? Will operator logs contain customer data/PII?
- Subprocessors: can you provide a current list of subprocessors engaged for private deployments (especially any cloud or managed-support partners)?
- Cross-border: any scenarios where metadata or logs may leave the US? We need assurance for our EU patients that data residency is preserved.

I've attached Medica's DPA checklist for reference (Medica-DPA-criteria.pdf).

Appreciate any clarifications — we can also set aside time for Legal + Security to meet.

Thanks,
Sara Holt\Director of IT Risk\Medica Health

--- attachment stub: Medica-DPA-criteria.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Holt <sara.holt@medicahealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 09 Jun 2025 12:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on private deployment privacy terms — keys & access

Sara — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front and then a suggested next step.

1) Key custody: we support customer-managed keys for both VPC and on-prem packages. Options: BYOK with customer CMKs (no Redwood escrow required), or Redwood-managed keys if the customer prefers. For BYOK, we can document key rotation and access policies in the DPA.

2) Operator access / breakglass: by default, no ongoing operator access to customer data. For breakglass/support we use a time-limited access workflow via a jump-host approved by the customer; all access is logged and must be pre-authorized by your security contact. We can provide an operator-access playbook that outlines the approval flows, notification windows, and audit artifacts.

3) Subprocessors: there is a small set for private deployments — primarily the managed-support partner we use for on-prem hardware fixtures and a logging/obs SaaS for aggregated metrics (both under strict contract). I'll have Security produce a current subprocessor list.

4) Cross-border: for VPC in the US region and on-prem installs, customer data and logs remain in-customer control; telemetry we request is minimal and can be configured to exclude content-level logs. If Medica needs contractual guarantees, we can add an export restriction clause to the DPA.

Next step: can we arrange a 30-minute call with your Security + Legal to walk through the DPA redlines and operator access playbook? Proposed times: Wed 11 Jun 10:00am PT or Thu 12 Jun 9:00am PT. I attached our ops matrix to show the typical separation of duties.

Thanks —
Stephanie Nguyen\Head of Sales, Healthcare 
Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Sara Holt <sara.holt@medicahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on private deployment privacy terms — keys & access

Looping in a couple of security/legal details so Medica has a concrete list. Monica and I talked through this and here's an exportable snapshot you can share with Medica Legal:

- Subprocessors (current): Managed Hardware Partner LLC (on-prem install support), ObservaMetrics Inc. (aggregated health of fleet telemetry), SecureShip Logistics (hardware transit for air-gapped installs). Full CSV attached.
- Data usage: Redwood does not train models on customer production data for private deployments; language model training is explicitly excluded in the DPA.
- Key escrow: we recommend customers hold CMKs in their KMS (no Redwood-hosted escrow). If legal/regulators require escrow, we can offer an isolated escrow service with split-control and writ-down processes — that would be a negotiated addendum.
- Logs and PII: operator-facing logs are redacted by default and contain operational metadata. Content-level logs (request/response bodies) are not included in standard operator logs; we can provide an auditable mechanism to filter or exclude PII from telemetry exports.

Action: Rishi will prepare a redline of the DPA with the export restriction and the operator-access SOW. Recommend we deliver the redline by Fri 13 Jun.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra\Head of Security Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Sara Holt <sara.holt@medicahealth.com>

Date: Thu, 12 Jun 2025 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on private deployment privacy terms — keys & access

Stephanie / Rishi — this is helpful, thank you. A few follow-ups from Legal and Security after reviewing:

- Breakglass: Legal wants a documented SLA on notification timing and customer approval path (eg, email + ticket + 2nd contact) before any operator session. Can Redwood commit to a maximum 4-hour window for remedial access once authorized?
- Logs: we need written confirmation that operator logs will not include patient PII under any normal or breakglass access. If redaction is not feasible in all cases, we need a contractual commitment to destroy any inadvertently captured PII and a notification process.
- Jurisdiction: confirm that for a US-region VPC or on-prem install, logs and metadata will not be transferred outside the US unless we explicitly request it.

If Rishi can share the redline Friday, Legal will review and aim to return comments within 5 business days. Also, please include your proposed emergency access playbook in the package so our security team can vet the steps.

Best,
Sara

Sara — appreciate the quick turn from Legal. Summary of commitments and next steps below:

Committed items:
- Breakglass timing: Redwood will adopt a documented notification workflow; for remedial support sessions we commit to a maximum 4-hour approval-to-access SLA when customer approval is provided (subject to pre-authorized emergency contact list).
- Operator logs: Operator audit logs are redacted by default and do not contain request/response content. If PII is captured inadvertently during a breakglass session, Redwood will delete the captured content within 72 hours and notify Medica Legal within 48 hours of discovery. We will include this clause in the DPA redline.
- Jurisdiction: For US-region VPC and on-prem deployments, logs and customer metadata will remain in customer-controlled infrastructure. Any telemetry that leaves the environment is opt-in and can be contractually restricted.

Deliverables and timeline:
- Rishi to deliver DPA redline (including export restriction and operator access SOW) by EOD Fri 13 Jun — attached here: RDW-DPA-redline-20250613.pdf
- Operator access playbook attached for review: operator-access-playbook.pdf
- Proposed short call to finalize: Mon 16 Jun 9:00am PT (30 mins). If that works, I'll send a calendar invite for Security + Legal.

Let me know if you want the redline as tracked-changes in a Google Doc instead — we can put the doc in the shared Drive link.

Thanks again — looking forward to getting this across the finish line.

Best,
